description: Production dictionary for original distributor statement sheets/files and reporting dimensions. It explains each source before account policies decide whether rows enter catalog, statement, cash or audit views. Raw fields remain immutable.

reporting_dimensions.purpose: Normalize distributor vocabulary once so every report can use the same DSP, monetization and content-origin dimensions without changing raw data or amounts.

classification_status_values.exact: The source explicitly supports DSP, monetization and origin.
classification_status_values.partial: The DSP is known but at least one secondary dimension is not explicit.
classification_status_values.unknown: The source does not provide enough evidence. No inference is allowed.

guardrails: Account policies continue to decide generation, cash, transfer and audit inclusion.
Shares In & Out never become generation because of store normalization.
Original distributor columns are preserved without rewriting.
Altafonte legacy remains Unknown when the original row lacks store evidence.
Unknown values remain Unknown; reports must not invent a more precise origin.

entries.human_description: Detalle mensual de ADA por ISRC, DSP, territorio, modalidad e importe. Los TXT sin actividad son statements validos pero no generan filas economicas.
entries.period_column: statement date in filename, validated with Start Period and End Period
entries.decision_reason: Net Royalty Payable is the real amount after ADA Deductible Fees. Royalty Payable and fees are retained separately for exact reconciliation.
entries.known_risks: Repdate Month ID is consumption/reporting activity and can precede the settlement month. Do not use it as statement_period. No-activity TXT files must not be treated as missing statements.

entries.human_name: ADA Indyana Records royalty detail TXT
entries.human_description: Detalle mensual de la cuenta ADA 99500 / Indyana Records LLC por ISRC, DSP, territorio, modalidad e importe.
entries.period_column: statement date in filename, validated with Start Period and End Period
entries.decision_reason: Net Royalty Payable is the real amount after ADA Deductible Fees. The original Account 99500 identifies Indyana Records and remains preserved in raw columns.
entries.known_risks: Repdate Month ID can precede the statement month. Account 99500 must not be merged with ADA Mawz account 99205.

entries.human_description: Detailed FUGA royalty rows by product/asset. This is the main FUGA generation detail.
entries.decision_reason: Reported Royalty is the real income field. Currency is treated as EUR in the existing validated FUGA logic and converted through monthly FX.
entries.known_risks: Some YouTube/UGC rows can miss ISRC or artist fields. FUGA correction files must be controlled separately.

entries.human_description: FUGA correction file used to adjust prior reporting. It is not a normal recurring statement, but can contain valid income/correction rows.
entries.decision_reason: Corrections are part of the validated FUGA result but require explicit traceability because they do not behave like ordinary monthly files.
entries.known_risks: Correction file names may not carry a normal statement month. Avoid treating every correction as a standard recurring statement.

entries.human_description: DashGo detailed royalty rows used for statements and catalog discovery.
entries.decision_reason: DashGo was validated against the old pipeline with diff approximately zero.
entries.known_risks: Keep original detail columns available for future store/territory/usage checks.

entries.human_description: Orchard detailed revenue rows. Historical Altafonte data is mapped into the Orchard business flow where possible.
entries.decision_reason: Orchard is treated as a direct generation statement. Altafonte historical rows are legacy but belong to the same business continuity.
entries.known_risks: Historical Altafonte files can be less structured. Keep legacy rows traceable.

entries.human_description: SoundOn royalty detail used as the valid income source.
entries.decision_reason: SoundOn summary files are not used as royalties; my_royalty detail is the accepted source.
entries.known_risks: Do not double count summary files.

entries.human_description: SoundOn summary/aggregate files. Useful for orientation only, not detail royalty rows.
entries.decision_reason: Summary files can double count or duplicate my_royalty detail and should not enter royalty marts.
entries.known_risks: Loading summaries as royalty rows would inflate reports.

entries.human_description: Master/catalog generation detail. This is the primary source for measuring what a master generated before interpreting share transfers.
entries.decision_reason: Masters represent generation. Whether it belongs to VPO depends on account policy and catalog/contract cutoff.
entries.known_risks: For external/mixed accounts, Masters can include old artist catalog that is not VPO business.

entries.human_description: YouTube channel/video income detail. It can represent generation but often lacks ISRC and requires video/title identifiers.
entries.decision_reason: YouTube income is generation when tied to the business scope, but may need catalog matching because IDs differ from Masters.
entries.known_risks: Missing ISRC can cause incorrect contract cutoff if matching only by month.

entries.human_description: Share participation movements between accounts. This is not master generation by itself.
entries.decision_reason: Shares can be relevant for cash/audit but should not be summed as generation in the new statement report.
entries.known_risks: Adding Shares to Masters can mix generation with transfers and distort report totals.

entries.human_description: Statement summary page if present. Useful for reconciliation but not a detail mart source.
entries.decision_reason: Summaries should not be loaded as detailed royalty rows.
entries.known_risks: Double counting if summary and detail are both summed.
